newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end square after mixed session. [CORRECTED 6:26 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end square after mixed session. [CORRECTED 6:26 GMT]

text.p: * New Zealand share prices end almost exactly square
* Lion, Telecom edge ahead
* Media stocks Wilson & Horton, INL, outperform
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
(Corrects NZSE-40 Cap Index)
305 +1 * NZSC cap index +2.36 at 5,043.70
332 +2 * Volume NZ$56 million. Futures -1 at 1,094
650 +1 * Other movers - +55 +12
New Zealand share prices ended almost exactly square on Wednesday with Telecom again dominating turnover and the market ignoring the U.S. Federal Reserve's quarter point rate hike overnight.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended just 0.60 of a point higher at 2,220.87 (Corrects). Turnover was worth NZ$56 million, with Telecom again representing about half of that.
The first round of Telecom's share buy back ends on Thursday.
Lion Nathan was actively traded, 2.52 million shares trading for NZ$8.3 million.
Brokers said rumours that Tony O'Reilly's Independent Newspapers was seeking the remaining 15 percent of Wilson and Horton were behind W&H's 55-cent gain to NZ$11.80.
Total turnover in the stock was NZ$838,308, the biggest parcel being 25,000 shares sold at the closing price.
Brokers were treating the talk with scepticism, but they noted W&H attracted reasonable turnover last week.
They also noted that, with both W&H and INP having recently released their financial results, such a move might be timely from a disclosure perspective.
Both posted modest gains, Telecom gaining one to NZ$6.50 and Lion Nathan two to NZ$3.32.

"Our market is still a very thin market. Technically the market is probably underpinned at around about the 2,200 level," Peter Lynds at ANZ Securities said. "It's more or less waiting for a lead," Lynds said.
Richard Burton at Cavill White Securities said the big cap issues were again dominating business, but the market was otherwise lacklustre.
